name: spot-project-request-to-notion

trigger.authentication_note: Solution Partner Operations Tool connection 'work.flowers'. The partner-tool credential lives HERE, on the trigger — the workflow code never calls the partner tool, so it is not in --connections.
trigger.trigger_note: Polling trigger, one run per new project request. Claimed 2026-07-31 with status 'active' and zero runs — DELIBERATELY claimed BEFORE Zapier's ~2026-08-03 cutover of directory lead delivery onto SPOT. A polling trigger banks its first poll after being claimed as already-seen rather than firing it, so claiming after the cutover risked swallowing the first real request as backlog. Nothing before the cutover can fire it, so claiming early cost nothing.

tables.01KYV1R8BWAZ697HQ8P1QV80AF: SPOT Project Requests — request id -> the Notion Deal/Contact/Company page ids it produced, plus the raw payload. Owned by this Zap; the dedupe key that makes a retry or re-poll a no-op. 'Created On' is a Text field, not Date & Time, because Tables coerces a bare YYYY-MM-DD into the account timezone and stores the previous day.
tables.01JYEPSEARXB2Z6BJRCMFGXBC2: email -> Notion Contact page id, owned by contact-emails-to-zapier-table. Read here, and written when this Zap creates a contact.
tables.01JM8PH8YM93A482M8BFZ6WKW6: Notion Companies mirror, owned by notion-companies-to-zapier-table (read-only here; the domain -> company page id lookup).

notion_data_sources.21991b07-11ac-81a6-a894-000be4a09a67: Contacts — found by email or created. Country is stored as a FULL NAME here (64 options).
notion_data_sources.21991b07-11ac-80b0-b787-000b3d3995f6: Companies — resolved by domain or created. Country is stored as ISO ALPHA-2 here (8 options), so a full name must be mapped down; writing 'United States' would mint a ninth option beside 'US'.
notion_data_sources.21a91b07-11ac-808d-9657-000b1390d20b: Deals — always created, one per request. Its default template already sets Status=Lead and Owner, so this Zap never writes a status-typed property.

partner_app.note: Solution Partner Operations Tool (SPOT; private, invite-only). Sibling triggers referral_lead_status_change (used by zapier-partner-lead-status-to-notion) and updated_project_request (unused — the natural phase-2 sibling that would move the Deal's Status along the pipeline).

description: New Zapier Solution Partner project request -> upsert a Notion Contact, Company and Deal. Company resolves via the companies mirror Table by domain, then the contact's existing Related Company, then a live Notion query by Website, then create. An existing Contact is only filled in, never overwritten. The Deal opens at Lead from the Deals default template; Type, Value and Expected Close are left for whoever scopes it, and Status is never written on an existing Deal so a human's Declined cannot be undone. Raw payload preserved on the Deal page, in the request Table and in the run output.
durable_version_note: Pinned to 0.10.1, matching both sibling partner Zaps. A publish on 0.11.0 failed at run time with 'Dependency installation failed' — the durable runtime's pnpm enforces a 24-hour minimum release age. The same guard applies to @zapier/zapier-sdk and zod; check a version's publish date before bumping any of the three.

unexercised.state: Published and enabled, trigger active, ZERO runs. Nothing in this workflow has executed.
unexercised.why: The trigger has never carried a payload: directory requests arrived as PartnerPage emails until Zapier's ~2026-08-03 cutover. Published ahead of it deliberately (see trigger_note).
unproven: The payload key SPELLINGS. The field SET is evidenced from the last PartnerPage delivery, but the snake_case keys SPOT uses are inferred, so extractRequest reads each field from a candidate list.

The `properties|||<name>|||<type>` key forms for Primary Phone (phone_number), Country (select, both data sources), Account Owner Email Override (email) and First Contacted (date__start). These are addressed through create_database_item's CACHED schema, which could not be resolved from the publishing session — the Zapier MCP server's own Notion connection returned an empty dynamic_properties_schema for these data sources, which means it cannot see them, NOT that the keys are wrong.
first_run_checklist: Read the run output: it echoes the raw payload, so the true key spellings are readable without opening Notion.
Check the Deal page body's 'Raw request payload' block against the mapped properties — an empty property with a populated payload key means a candidate spelling missed.
Confirm no new select option appeared on Companies Country / Industry / Size or Contacts Country.
